channel.title: ExeBrowser — new games and posts

item.title: New game: Archive Extractor
item.description: Drop an archive, browse it, pull out what you need. Nothing uploads and nothing installs.

item.title: Why Won't My Old Program Run on Windows 11?
item.description: Six reasons old Windows software stops working on Windows 11 — missing 16-bit support, dead runtimes, broken installers, retired copy protection — and what actually fixes each one.

item.title: Open Cadet: Space Cadet Pinball, Fully Open Source
item.description: 3D Pinball Space Cadet needs a proprietary PINBALL.DAT to run. I rebuilt that data file from scratch — original art, 47 synthesized sounds, CC0 public domain — so the open-source engine finally runs with zero Microsoft files. Here's how.

item.title: How to Extract Files From an Installer, Without Installing
item.description: Old setup.exe won't run, but you just need the files inside? Here's how to unpack a legacy Windows installer — with 7-Zip, innoextract, cabextract, msiextract, or a browser sandbox — without a full install.

item.title: Where to Legally Get Classic Windows and DOS Games in 2026
item.description: An honest guide to legally free classic PC games in 2026: redistributable shareware, official freeware, open-source remakes, licensed storefronts — and the truth about abandonware.

item.title: Running 16-bit Windows 3.x Software in 2026
item.description: Why 16-bit Windows 3.x programs won't start on 64-bit Windows at all — and four honest ways to run them in 2026, including right in a browser tab.

item.title: We Tested 50+ Windows Apps in the Browser — What Runs
item.description: We ran more than 50 classic Windows and DOS programs through a browser-based Wine + DOSBox runtime and logged the results. Here's the full table: what plays instantly, what's partial, and what won't run.

item.title: How to Run Windows Software on a Chromebook (4 Ways)
item.description: Four realistic ways to run Windows programs on a Chromebook, ranked by effort: a no-install browser tool, Linux + Wine, remote desktop, and cloud Windows.

item.title: Wine vs. an Emulator: What's the Difference?
item.description: Wine is famously 'not an emulator' — what that means, how it differs from DOSBox-style emulation, and why running Windows apps in a browser needs both.

item.title: How to Run Old Windows Software Without a Virtual Machine
item.description: You don't always need a virtual machine to run an old Windows program. When a browser-based Wine tool is enough, when a VM is still the right call, and how to decide quickly.
